title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a stratified space whose strata X_i^* are indexed by a finite poset I. For each flag d = (i_0 < ... < i_k) of strata there is a 'deployed' space Σ_d. Up to homotopy this is the iterated link, or homotopy link, of the flag. For a single stratum, Σ_i is the deployed stratum: the stratum truncated by removing open tubes around the smaller strata. The problem served is the 'déploiement' of a stratified space: replacing it by a diagram of manifold-like pieces indexed by flags, glued along boundaries. This is the programme later announced in the Esquisse (§5–6, tame topology and dévissage).

Previous page. For J ⊂ I' with L = I' \ J nonempty, Grothendieck takes the tubular neighbourhood T_{Σ_J,Σ_{I'}} of Σ_J inside Σ_{I'} and its boundary Ṫ. He defines Σ^♮_{J,L} as the part of that boundary lying in Σ_L. He conjectures in (78) that Σ^♮_{J,L} ≅ colim Σ_d, the colimit taken over flags d of J∪L whose first term lies in J and whose last term lies in L. He then gives the maps in (79): the canonical inclusion Σ_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L and the projection Σ_{J,L} → Σ_J induced by the tube retraction.

This page.
- Making (79) explicit via (78). Because J lies 'below' L (J is the closed or initial part, L its complement in I'), every flag occurring in (78) splits uniquely as (j_1…j_p l_1…l_q), with j's in J, l's in L and p, q ≥ 1. This is formula (80).
- Formula (81). For such a flag there is an inclusion Σ_{j_1…j_p l_1…l_q} ↪ Σ_{l_1…l_q} and a projection Σ_{j_1…j_p l_1…l_q} → Σ_{j_1…j_p}. These are the face maps 'forget the J-part' and 'forget the L-part'. They are compatible with the colimit and induce the two maps of (79).
- The Remark. The Σ_{J,L}, and the inclusions Σ_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L, have an intrinsic meaning, 'in a suitable isotopy category'. They are independent of the choice of local conical retractions around the strata X_i^*, at least in tame ('modérée') topology, and the description given here suits that setting. By contrast, the structure map Σ_{J,L} → Σ_J uses local tubular/conical structures. When local conical structures are available it is more convenient … (sentence cut off). The parenthesis says that in tame topology such structures are presumably guaranteed for 'quasi-…' spaces and are an additional 'tame' datum.

In modern terms this is the face and degeneracy structure of the diagram of homotopy links over the flag (subdivision) category of the stratification poset. It is also the observation that the link-boundary inclusions are canonical up to isotopy, while the bundle projections onto smaller strata depend on control or tubular data.
errors: Formula (78) is itself only conjectural ('sauf erreur'). The explicit description here inherits that status.

The unique decomposition (80) needs J to be an initial (down-closed) segment of I', with L its complement, so that in any flag all J-terms precede all L-terms. This is implicit in the setup but not stated on this page.
The remark is cut off mid-sentence; the convenient alternative construction promised when conical structures exist is on a missing next page.

ideas.what: Unique splitting of flags of J∪L into a J-part followed by an L-part, giving the maps Σ_{jl} → Σ_j and Σ_{jl} ↪ Σ_l between deployed pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Face maps of the homotopy-link diagram over the flag poset (sd(P)); join decomposition of flags
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Woolf; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping / links of conically smooth stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of dévissage of stratified tame spaces is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6

ideas.what: Intrinsic (isotopy-invariant) nature of the link-boundary pieces Σ_{J,L} and of the inclusions Σ_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L, versus dependence of the projection Σ_{J,L} → Σ_J on local conical or tubular structures.
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of regular neighbourhoods / conical structures up to isotopy; control data (Thom–Mather); canonical holink evaluation maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data), Siebenmann (uniqueness of conical structures up to isotopy, 1972), Quinn
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses the uniqueness up to isotopy of tubular/dévissage structures in tame topology, only at the level of the announcement

ideas.what: Working 'in a suitable isotopy category' of tame spaces, in which deployed structures are canonical.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy-coherent / ∞-categorical treatment of stratified spaces (exit-path ∞-categories, conically smooth spaces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly separates which parts of the deployment are intrinsic (the Σ_{J,L} and their inclusions into Σ_L, up to isotopy) from which need extra conical/tubular data (the projections to Σ_J). He was heading toward a more convenient formalism once local conical structures are given, but the text breaks off.
missed.quote: Les Σ_{J,L} ont un sens intrinsèque … ainsi que les Σ_{J,L} ↪ Σ_L … la structure Σ_{J,L} → Σ_J par contre utilise les [structures] tubulaires locales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This matches what modern theories (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzipping, Lurie's exit-paths, Quinn holinks) handle by passing to homotopy links, where the projection becomes canonical. It is a historical anticipation rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine bookkeeping step (splitting flags, face maps) in Grothendieck's unpublished deployment of stratified spaces. The remark on intrinsic versus structure-dependent maps is a sound and perceptive anticipation of later conically smooth / homotopy-link theory, but it is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The circled insertion '(dans une catégorie isotopique convenable)' belongs to the Remark ('ont un sens intrinsèque (dans une catégorie isotopique convenable)'), not to diagram (81).
The superscript insertion reads roughly 'intervenant dans (78)' (i.e. 'tout drapeau de J∪L intervenant dans (78)'), not 'l'intervalle des (78)'.
'donnement des rétractions coniques locales autour des X_i^*' should read 'indépendamment des rétractions coniques locales autour des X_i^*'.
The duplicated line 'des X_i^*, des maps[?] en théorie topologique' should read 'des X_i^*, du moins en théorie topologique modérée'.

'la structure Σ_{J,L} → Σ_J' is preceded by 'et la description que j'en ai donnée ici est adaptée à ce cas –'. The crossed-out words are 'structures coniques' (or 'dévissages coniques'), replaced by an inserted word that looks like 'tubulaires'.
The page writes Σ_{J,L}, without the ♮ used on the previous page, in the Remark.
(81) is a diagram with a horizontal inclusion to Σ_{l_1…l_q} and a vertical arrow down to Σ_{j_1…j_p}, as transcribed.
